request.query: Register as a resident and get a Finnish personal identity code (DVV)

sources.title: dvv.fi
highlights: You can get a personal identity code if you are residing legally in Finland and there are grounds for registration, such as
a valid passport or an official photo ID card of a citizen from an EU member country, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, or San Marino
a residence permit card or any other possible proof that you are residing legally in Finland
proof of work or studies in Finland, for example, a certificate of student status or an employment contract (employee, check your right to work

sources.title: dvv.fi
highlights: A personal identity code is issued to a foreign citizen moving to Finland from abroad after they have been registered in the Population Information System at their own request or at the time they are granted a residence permit
A personal identity code is issued to a person who is registered in Finland’s Population Information System

sources.title: suomi.fi
highlights: After submitting the form, you must visit our service location in person

sources.title: finlandhandbook.com
highlights: If you submit your request in August or early September, expect the DVV processing times to stretch toward the 4-to-6-week mark
If you have the flexibility to travel, sometimes booking an appointment at a DVV office in a smaller town like Porvoo, Lahti, or even further afield can shave weeks off your wait for an appointment

sources.title: nordicexpat.com
highlights: Book as early as you can; if slots are scarce, check service points in nearby municipalities and the booking system at different times of day

sources.title: nordicexpat.com
highlights: If family registration matters to you, check DVV's document requirements in advance — this is the single most common cause of a wasted appointment

sources.title: relocateineurope.com
highlights: Registration cannot be sped up except for very weighty reasons; opening a bank account is not one

sources.title: nordicexpat.com
highlights: If your code has not arrived yet but you are about to start work, ask whether a tax office near you can issue a personal identity code, so you are not stuck on the 60% rate
